General information.Name: EPD: SANDWICH PANELS ISODECK PVSTEEL TPO-PVC WITH STEEL FACINGS AND INSULATING CORE OF POLYURETHAN OR POLYSOCINURATE FOAM
General information.Category: Manufacturing/332 Fabricated Metal Product Manufacturing/332311 Prefabricated Metal Building and Component Manufacturing
General information.Description: Environmental Product Declaration for 1 m² of Isodeck PVSteel PU - PVC insulating roof panel with an insulation thickness of 80 mm and steel sheet thickness of 0.8 mm (external with membrane) + 0.5 mm (internal). The study follows a 'cradle-to-gate with options' approach, including modules A1-A5 (product stage, construction), C1-C4 (end-of-life), and D (benefits and loads beyond the system boundary). The panel consists of two external pre-painted galvanized steel supports enclosing an insulating core of polyurethane or polyisocyanurate foam. The results of this EPD are also applicable to the Isodeck PVSteel PU TPO (with the same insulation core thickness and sheet metal).
General information.Tags: EPD, sandwich panel, Isodeck PVSteel, building envelope, roof panel, polyurethane, polyisocyanurate, steel facing, construction
General information.Technology Description: The production process is continuous and involves: profiling of pre-painted galvanized steel coils; foaming, where chemical components are mixed and applied between the steel sheets and matured in a heated press; panel cutting and stacking; and packaging. The Life Cycle Assessment was performed using SimaPro 9.3.0.3 software with the Ecoinvent 3.7 database, in accordance with ISO 14025 and EN 15804.

processDocumentation.LCI method: In accordance with ISO 14025:2006 and EN 15804:2012+A2:2019/AC:2021
processDocumentation.Process type: Cradle-to-gate with options EPD for a manufactured construction product
processDocumentation.Modeling constants: Cut-off criterion of 1% maximum for the contributions of material and energy. The sum of excluded material inputs does not exceed 1% of the total material inputs. Energy and material consumption allocated based on annual production.
processDocumentation.Data source information: Primary data from Isopan Ibérica (Spain), Isopan Est (Romania), and Isopan Deutschland (Germany). Secondary data from databases: Ecoinvent 3.7, World Steel Association, Plastics Europe.
processDocumentation.Data completeness: The sum of excluded material inputs does not exceed 1% of the total material inputs. To the knowledge of the authors of the LCA study no exclusions have been made.
processDocumentation.Data selection: Cut-off criterion of 1% maximum for material and energy contributions.
processDocumentation.Data treatment: Energy and material consumption have been allocated to the specific product based on the annual production of the panels.
processDocumentation.Sampling procedure: Data collected from three production plants for the reference year.
processDocumentation.Use advice: EPDs within the same product category but registered in different EPD programmes may not be comparable. EPDs of construction products may not be comparable if they do not comply with EN 15804.
processDocumentation.Completeness: High, based on a 1% cut-off rule and inclusion of all known relevant flows for the declared scope.
processDocumentation.Sources: GENERAL PROGRAMME INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE INTERNATIONAL EPD® SYSTEM, VER 4.0 (2021-02-29); PCR 2019:14 version 1.2.5, 2022-11-01 'Construction products'; ΕΝ 15804:2012 + A2:2019; UNI EN ISO 14025:2010; UNI EN ISO 14040:2021; UNI EN ISO 14044:2021; UNI EN 16783:2017; c-PCR-005 Thermal Insulation products (EN 16783); Life Cycle Assessment Technical Report, October 2022 - Bureau Veritas Nexta Srl
processDocumentation.Intended application: Insulating panels for roofs of industrial, commercial, civil buildings, animal husbandry and cold stores.
